children: The ₹351-crore Initial Public Offering (IPO) of Mumbai-based real estate developer Pranav Constructions Ltd. will open for subscription on Monday, September 7. The three-day bidding window will close on September 9.
Ahead of the issue opening, the company raised ₹84.2 crore from nine anchor investors, including Goldman Sachs Investments (Mauritius), ITI Mutual Fund and Taurus Mutual Fund.
Pranav Constructions, promoted by Pranav Kiran Ashar and Ravi Ramalingam, on Friday allotted 67.94 lakh equity shares to anchor investors at the upper end of the price band of ₹118-124 per share.
Goldman Sachs Investments (Mauritius) emerged as the largest investor in the anchor book, acquiring 20.16 lakh shares for ₹25 crore.

Of the total anchor allocation, 19.75 lakh equity shares were allotted to ITI Mutual Fund and Taurus Mutual Fund through seven schemes. Other investors in the anchor book included Abudantia Capital, Ashika India Select Fund, Asio Fund, Rigel Global Fund and Saint Capital Fund.
Pranav Constructions IPO: Should you apply?
SBI Securities has recommended subscribing to the issue at the cut-off price, citing the company’s asset-light model, superior return profile, improving balance sheet and scalable business model.

According to the brokerage, Pranav Constructions is a leading Mumbai Metropolitan Region (MMR) redevelopment player, with Revenue, EBITDA and PAT CAGR of 30.5%, 49.5% and 34.2%, respectively, between FY24 and FY26. Its RoCE and RoE stood at 25.1% and 28.9%, respectively.

The company has also significantly deleveraged its balance sheet, with borrowings declining from ₹538 crore in FY26 to ₹236 crore as of July 2026. SBI Securities expects the post-issue debt-to-equity ratio to decline to around 0.3x from around 1.1x.

The brokerage said a strong pipeline of 37 projects with an aggregate total developable area (TDA) of 3.6 million square feet, the addition of 7-8 projects annually and high entry barriers in redevelopment position the company to benefit from the growing MMR redevelopment opportunity.

The company’s brand also supports pre-sales, with around 60% of sales taking place within the first year of launch, according to SBI Securities. At the upper price band of ₹124, the issue is valued at 19.6x FY26 post-issue P/E and 2.2x market capitalisation to pre-sales, which the brokerage considers attractive compared with most listed peers.

BP Equities has also assigned a 'SUBSCRIBE' rating to the issue, citing Pranav Constructions’ pure-play focus on Mumbai redevelopment, strong financial performance, improving margins, favourable demand-supply dynamics and long-term growth prospects. The brokerage said the valuation is reasonable.
Pranav Constructions IPO: Issue details and use of proceeds
The price band has been fixed at ₹118-124 per share. Retail investors can bid for a minimum of 120 shares, requiring a minimum investment of ₹14,880 at the upper price band.

The IPO comprises a fresh issue of equity shares worth ₹315.6 crore and an offer for sale (OFS) of 28.56 lakh shares by existing investor BioUrja India Infra, worth ₹35.42 crore at the upper price band.

Pranav Constructions plans to use ₹145.7 crore of the net proceeds from the fresh issue towards redevelopment expenses, while ₹91.5 crore will be used for debt repayment. The remaining proceeds will be utilised for general corporate purposes.

The redevelopment expenses will include costs related to obtaining government and statutory approvals, purchasing additional floor space index (FSI), and compensating members for alternate accommodation and hardship compensation for certain under-construction and upcoming redevelopment projects.
65 redevelopment projects across MCGM region
Pranav Constructions operates primarily in the Mumbai suburban region and has a portfolio of 65 redevelopment projects across the Municipal Corporation of Greater Mumbai (MCGM) region.

The portfolio comprises 28 completed projects, 20 under-construction projects with a total developable area of 1.63 million square feet, and 17 upcoming projects with a total developable area of 1.96 million square feet.
Pranav Constructions financial performance
On the financial front, Pranav Constructions reported a profit of ₹71.3 crore for FY26, up 14.6% from ₹62.3 crore in FY25.
Revenue increased 19.7% year-on-year to ₹761.6 crore in FY26 from ₹636.3 crore in the previous fiscal year.
Pranav Constructions IPO: Risk factors

The company’s redevelopment business is geographically concentrated in the MCGM region, which accounted for 99.5%, 99.7% and 99.7% of redevelopment revenue in FY24, FY25 and FY26, respectively. This leaves the company exposed to economic conditions, real estate demand and regulatory developments specific to Mumbai.

Project execution is another key risk. As of March 2026, Pranav Constructions had 20 under-construction projects with a combined developable area of 1.63 million square feet and 17 upcoming projects covering 1.96 million square feet. Historically, completed redevelopment projects have taken an average of 26 months from the issuance of the first commencement certificate to the grant of the occupation certificate.

The company also faces inventory sales risk as rising property prices could weigh on affordability, particularly in affordable and mid-income housing segments. In FY26, the company had 611 units under construction, of which 75 remained unsold, compared with 432 units under construction and 90 unsold units in FY25.

Dependence on contractors is another risk, with the top 10 contractors accounting for 46.9%, 56.4% and 47.1% of total contractor payments in FY24, FY25 and FY26, respectively. Any disruption or delay involving these contractors could affect project timelines and financial performance.
Centrum Broking and PNB Investment Services are the merchant bankers to the public issue.

title: Pranav Constructions IPO opens today: Should you subscribe to the ₹351 crore issue?
